thread:
alex_infra: Heads up — between ~02:28-02:36 UTC we saw short spike windows of packet loss on vxlan overlay in us-west2 GPU clusters. Apps report 0.7-1.9% drop during ~30s windows, then clears. Any recent changes? :eyes:

morgan_sre: seeing similar alerts. Our p50 latency also jittered. Alerts from health checks + kube-probe failures. No full node reboots though.

alex_infra: attaching quick capture from node gpu-node-14 (small pcap excerpt):
```
17:28:31.123456 IP vxlan0 > 10.0.3.12: UDP, length 1420
17:28:31.123457 IP vxlan0 > 10.0.3.12: UDP, length 1420
17:28:31.154987 IP vxlan0 > 10.0.3.12: UDP, length 200
...
```

raghu_net: can you grep dmesg for mlx5/rdma errors? and paste `ip -s link show vxlan0` output. Also what MTU on underlay + pod iface?

alex_infra: dmesg ok — no mlx5 panic. ip -s link output:
```
vxlan0: mtu 1450 qdisc noop state UNKNOWN mode DEFAULT group default
    RX: bytes 12345678 packets 98765 errors 0 dropped 0
    TX: bytes 87654321 packets 87654 errors 0 dropped 13
```

liana_dev: dropped tx on vxlan0 (13) is interesting. Could be egress queue overflow from bursts when autoscaler backfilled GPUs overnight. We saw a backfill wave at 02:30.

sam_gpu: note: kernel on affected nodes is 5.15.21 vs stable fleet 5.15.10 — older driver differences for offloads. A few nodes had a recent kubelet restart during backfill.

morgan_sre: hypothesis: intermittent egress drops due to large burst + offload/GRO/GSO interaction on vxlan encapsulated packets. Can we reproduce with a controlled synthetic burst? e.g., `nping --udp --rate 8000` across pods. Also try toggling `ethtool -K eth0 gro off gso off tso off` on a test node.

alex_infra: trying reproduce now on staging GPU pool (same kernel). Running iperf3 UDP flood between two pods. Initial run shows sawtooth loss matching earlier window.

alex_infra: quick sysctl and ifconfig snapshot:
```
net.ipv4.tcp_mtu_probing = 0
net.core.rmem_max = 212992
eth0 mtu 9000
vxlan0 mtu 1450
```

raghu_net: mismatched MTU between underlay (9000) and overlay (1450) is expected due to encapsulation, but the kernel should handle. Check if any intermediate MTU path change happened (FRR/MP-BGP reconverge?) — run `tracepath` between the two nodes.

liana_dev: adding that the burst coincides with a scheduled nightly snapshot job that writes to a sidecar network volume — increases traffic on the node network. Could be aggregate burst tipping qdisc.

morgan_sre: action plan: 1) reproduce with synthetic burst 2) toggle GSO/GRO on isolated node 3) collect `tc -s qdisc` counters + `ss -s` 4) see if backfill/autoscaler timing correlates 5) if confirmed, try adjusting `fq_codel` qdisc or small MTU on vxlan to spread packetization.

sam_gpu: FYI RDMA (mlx5) stats show no RNR/err on those nodes. Offload path only. I can roll a canary with kernel 5.15.10 on two nodes and run the same bursts.

ci-bot: deploy-notice: rolling canary image `staging-encap-test:v3` to gpu-staging-3 started at 1753216805.

alex_infra: after toggling `ethtool -K eth0 gro off gso off tso off` on the test node, the synthetic burst lost ~0.1% vs 1.6% before. That points to offload/GRO aggregation bug under encapsulation.

morgan_sre: good repro. Open a kernel/offload bug with vendor (Mellanox) and schedule a mitigation: 1) mark affected nodes `no-gso` taint and drain for kernel rollback or 2) set systemd-tmpfiles or daemon to disable offloads at boot if vendor fix delayed.

raghu_net: also create BPF probe to count `skb->len` before and after vxlan encapsulate for a few minutes to quantify fragmentation/aggregation.

liana_dev: noting customer impact: small percent of model training jobs saw transient gRPC retries but finished — cost minimal but user-facing SLO blip. If we throttle backfill concurrency we might avoid hitting the tipping point.

alex_infra: created ticket INF-3125 tracking: reproduction logs, pcap, ethtool results, nodes list, kernel versions, proposed mitigation (disable GSO on affected nodes + small canary kernel rollback).

morgan_sre: next steps: raghu to file vendor ticket + attach pcap, sam to prepare kernel rollback canary, alex to roll daemon to disable GSO on affected nodes if vendor delays, liana to throttle backfill tonight. :thumbsup:

sam_gpu: I can stage kernel rollback tonight at 03:30 UTC on two nodes and run the iperf3 test.

alex_infra: thanks all — will follow up in INF-3125 and post results here. If you see more alerts, ping @channel. :bell:
